report_md:
# Crypto risk appetite — development report

**Verdict: dev pass.** The BTC 20/60-day risk-appetite switch earns **53.66%
CAGR / 52.33% max DD / 1.28 Sharpe** at 1 bp over 2016-2023. It beats the
published TQQQ CAGR bar (36.72%) at 1, 5 and 10 bp (53.66% / 52.12% / 50.21%),
has all three subperiods positive, and is strongly non-random (placebo 99th
percentile). It is the only one of the three families that clears every
pre-registered kill check. The caveats are real: 2022 is -42.4%, 2023 alone is
+310.4%, and the 60-day-only variant is weak. 2024-2026 is untouched.

## Development metrics

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Exposure | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | 53.66% | 52.33% | 1.28 | 1.85 | 39.9% | 100.0% | 201 | 1,152x |
| 5 bp | 52.12% | 52.94% | 1.25 | 1.82 | 39.9% | 100.0% | 201 | 1,088x |
| 10 bp | 50.21% | 53.68% | 1.22 | 1.77 | 39.9% | 100.0% | 201 | 1,013x |

There are **201 fills across 101 independent fill days** (about 25 fills and
13 events per year). This is just above the 100-fill / 30-event floor; the
strategy is a low-activity regime switch, not a high-turnover system. Average
weights are **8.9% QQQ (warm-up only), 47.7% TQQQ, 43.3% BIL**.

The cost drag is only 3.45 pp from 1 bp to 10 bp because the state changes are
infrequent and the book is binary. The result is not cost-fragile.

## Subperiods and years

| Window | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 32.78% | 30.62% | 1.20 |
| 2020-2021 | 107.81% | 30.46% | 1.69 |
| 2022-2023 | 52.58% | 52.02% | 1.09 |

| Year | Return |
|---|---:|
| 2016 | +4.0% |
| 2017 | +96.1% |
| 2018 | +15.9% |
| 2019 | +21.5% |
| 2020 | +173.3% |
| 2021 | +64.3% |
| 2022 | -42.4% |
| 2023 | +310.4% |

All three subperiods are positive, but the path is uneven. 2022 is -42.4%:
BTC had several bear-market rallies that flipped the signal to TQQQ before
further equity declines. 2023 is +310.4%: BTC momentum turned negative in
mid-July and stayed negative through late October, so the strategy held BIL
through the Aug-Oct QQQ drawdown and re-entered before the November-December
rally. Excluding 2023, the CAGR is **33.90%** with a 0.94 Sharpe.

The 2023 dependence is the main caveat. The strategy is not a smooth
all-weather compounder; it is a regime switch that can have a large single
year.

## Plateau (8 pre-registered cells)

| Windows | TQQQ z | BIL z | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **20/60** | **0.00** | **0.00** | **53.66%** | **52.3%** | **1.28** | **201** | **1,152x** |
| 20/60 | 0.00 | -0.25 | 46.71% | 61.3% | 1.15 | 389 | 2,373x |
| 20/60 | +0.25 | 0.00 | 51.18% | 57.0% | 1.35 | 393 | 2,546x |
| 20/60 | +0.25 | -0.25 | 44.58% | 65.3% | 1.21 | 455 | 2,918x |
| 20 only | 0.00 | 0.00 | 49.43% | 47.6% | 1.20 | 309 | 1,815x |
| 20 only | +0.25 | -0.25 | 46.09% | 56.8% | 1.22 | 509 | 3,193x |
| 60 only | 0.00 | 0.00 | 20.44% | 83.7% | 0.67 | 145 | 536x |
| 60 only | +0.25 | -0.25 | 31.09% | 72.8% | 0.91 | 281 | 1,115x |

The six 20/60-blend and 20-only cells span **44.58% to 53.66%**, all above the
1 bp bar. The 60-only cells collapse to 20.44% and 31.09% and breach the
drawdown bar (83.7% and 72.8%). The fast 20-day BTC leg is essential; the
60-day leg alone is not a viable risk-appetite signal. The primary is the best
cell, but it is also the mechanism centre (positive/negative trend, no neutral
band), not a corner selected after the fact.

The threshold neighbours show the expected trade-off: adding a neutral QQQ
band (`+0.25/-0.25`) lowers CAGR to 44.58% and raises DD to 65.3%, while
keeping more QQQ exposure. The binary switch is the better expression of this
signal.

## Placebo and static attribution

* **Circular-shift placebo (100 shifts):** median CAGR 16.7%, 95th percentile
  41.4%; the real 53.66% is above 99 of 100 shifts (percentile 0.99). Median
  placebo Sharpe 0.56 vs the real 1.28 (97th percentile). Median placebo max
  DD 69.1% vs the real 52.3%.
* **Static book at the average weights (8.9/47.7/43.3):** 24.55% CAGR / 53.6%
  DD / 0.83 Sharpe. The timing adds **29.11 pp** of CAGR and 0.45 Sharpe. This
  is the largest timing contribution of the three families.

## Correlation to the nine current winners

| Winner | Correlation |
|---|---:|
| ratio-froth | 0.566 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.624 |
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.670 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.544 |
| family-session-timing | 0.558 |
| family-short-reversal | 0.497 |
| family-rebalance-flow | 0.675 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | 0.415 |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.614 |

Range **0.42 to 0.67**. The highest are `family-rebalance-flow` (0.675) and
`relative-value-tqqq` (0.670); the lowest is
`family-intraday-microstructure-day` (0.415). No correlation approaches 0.95.
Daily-return correlation with the other two new families is 0.59 (sector) and
0.51 (breadth).

A same-map **QQQ 20/60 momentum** control (binary TQQQ/BIL) earns 28.64% CAGR /
64.3% DD / 0.87 Sharpe and correlates **0.582** with this strategy. The BTC
signal adds 25.0 pp of CAGR; it is not a QQQ price-trend proxy. The correlation
is moderate because both are risk-on/off switches, but the timing and the
magnitude are different.

## Kill criteria

| Criterion | Result | Pass? |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 53.66% | yes |
| 1 bp max DD < 82.29% | 52.33% | yes |
| 10 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 50.21% | yes |
| Placebo percentile >= 90% | 99% | yes |
| Max winner correlation <= 0.95 | 0.675 | yes |
| >= 100 fills / >= 30 events | 201 / 101 | yes |
| No negative subperiod | all positive | yes |
| Static blend not within 1 pp | 24.55% vs 53.66% | yes |
| Causality audit | 25/25 perturb, 25/25 mapping | yes |

The verdict is **dev_pass**. The margin over the TQQQ bar is 16.9 pp at 1 bp
and 13.5 pp at 10 bp, so this is not a marginal pass.

## Caveats

* **2023 dependence.** 2023 is +310.4%; excluding it, CAGR is 33.90% and
  Sharpe 0.94. The full-window headline is flattered by one exceptional year.
* **2022 drawdown.** -42.4% in 2022. BTC bear-market rallies repeatedly turned
  the signal on before equity declines resumed. The max DD is 52.3%, not a
  crash-proof profile.
* **The 60-day-only variant fails.** 20.44% CAGR / 83.7% DD. The fast 20-day
  leg carries the edge; this is a fast risk-appetite switch, not a slow trend.
* **Activity is just above the floor.** 201 fills / 101 events. A slightly
  slower signal would fall below the 100-fill floor.
* **Timestamp correction.** The one-session BTC lag is required because Yahoo
  BTC daily bars close after the US equity close. Without the lag the result
  is higher; that version is not causal and is not used.
* **2016 is a warm-up year.** The z-score needs about 180 sessions, so early
  2016 is QQQ; +4.0% is not a full TQQQ year.
* **No crypto position.** BTC is a signal series only; the traded assets are
  QQQ, TQQQ and BIL.
* **Development only.** No 2024-2026 data was read.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd research/new/family-crypto-risk-appetite
python strategy.py        # rewrites result.json
```

`build_weights(ts, opens, closes)` returns `(n, 3)` minute weights and accepts
either the shared minute panel or a daily panel. The development guard rejects
panels extending past 2023-12-29 unless the caller supplies `end`.
hypothesis_md:
# family-crypto-risk-appetite — hypothesis and pre-registration

**Slug:** `family-crypto-risk-appetite`
**Family:** crypto risk appetite (BTC trend as an external switch)
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 only. 2024-2026 is not
loaded or inspected by the development run.
**Benchmark bar:** TQQQ 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe (published
1-minute-mark bar). TQQQ on this panel is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80.

## 1. Mechanism

Bitcoin is a 24/7, high-beta risk asset with a much faster and more
unconditional risk cycle than US equities. Its trend is not a QQQ price trend:
BTC can rally through an equity drawdown, and it can crash while QQQ is flat.
That makes BTC daily momentum a candidate external **risk-appetite** series.

When BTC's 20/60-day trend is positive, global risk appetite is expanding and
a 3x Nasdaq position is better compensated. When BTC's trend is negative,
risk appetite is contracting; the strategy holds T-bills rather than trying to
distinguish an equity-only pullback from a broader de-risking. The strategy
never trades crypto and never holds a crypto position. BTC is a signal series
only.

The primary object is **BTC-USD's 20/60-day price momentum**, not a QQQ moving
average, a volatility estimate, or a calendar clock. The 20-day leg captures
the fast risk pulse; the 60-day leg confirms the trend. Both are z-scored
against their own trailing 252-session distributions.

## 2. Exact rules

All inputs use BTC daily closes through session `t-1`. The target is set at the
close of session `t` and executed at the first bar open of `t+1`. The shared
2% band applies.

Let `b_t = log(BTC_t)`, and let `b_{t-1}` be the BTC close aligned to the prior
QQQ session.

1. `m20_t = b_{t-1} - b_{t-21}` and `m60_t = b_{t-1} - b_{t-61}`.
2. `z20_t` is the z-score of `m20_t` against its trailing 252 sessions
   (minimum 120); `z60_t` is the same for `m60_t`.
3. `score_t = (z20_t + z60_t) / 2`.
4. State:
   * **TQQQ** if `score_t > 0`;
   * **BIL** if `score_t <= 0`;
   * **QQQ** only during the warm-up, when the score is not finite.
5. Weights are long-only fractions of equity and sum to 1.

## 3. Data, decision clock, and causality

| Item | Choice |
|---|---|
| Signal | BTC-USD adjusted daily closes from `data/external/` |
| Execution | local 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel via `research/bt.py` |
| Session calendar | QQQ regular sessions; BTC reindexed/ffilled |
| Decision | close of session `t` |
| BTC lag | **one QQQ session**: the signal at `t` uses BTC closes through `t-1` |
| Fill | first bar open of `t+1` |
| Costs | 1 bp headline, 5 bp and 10 bp reported |
| Band | 2% notional |
| Crypto trading | none |

The one-session lag is not a tuning parameter; it is a timestamp correction.
Yahoo's BTC-USD daily bar for date `d` closes at 00:00 UTC of `d+1`, which is
19:00/20:00 ET on `d` and therefore **after** the 16:00 ET US equity close. At
the close of session `t`, the last completed BTC daily bar is `t-1`. Using the
BTC bar dated `t` at the equity close would be look-ahead. The strategy uses
`t-1` and is therefore causal. A future-value perturbation audit that replaces
every BTC value from session `t` onward with garbage confirms that the target
at `t` does not change.

The development run uses a panel that ends 2023-12-29. The external loader
reindexes to that panel's sessions, so no 2024-2026 price enters the signal or
the performance.

## 4. Why this is not an existing family

* Not a QQQ/TQQQ price trend: the signal is BTC's trend, a different asset
  with a different risk cycle. A same-map QQQ 20/60 momentum control is
  reported alongside the result; it earns materially less and is only
  moderately correlated.
* Not `ratio-froth` or `relative-value-tqqq`: there is no TQQQ/QQQ ratio, no
  ratio momentum, and no QQQ moving-average gate.
* Not `qqq-spy-relative`, `family-sector-rotation`, or `family-breadth`: no
  equity cross-section is used.
* Not a volatility target or a drawdown event: the position is a binary
  risk-on/risk-off state driven by the BTC momentum sign, not by realised
  volatility or a peak-to-trough trigger.
* Not a calendar clock, opening-range signal, or ML model.
* The 252-session window is only a standardization lookback for the 20/60-day
  momentum; it is not a 100-250 day price-trend gate.

## 5. Pre-registered 8-cell sensitivity grid

The grid includes the primary, three threshold neighbours at the 20/60 blend,
and the two single-horizon alternatives at two settings.

| Cell | Windows | TQQQ z | BIL z |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| **1 (primary)** | **20/60 blend** | **0.00** | **0.00** |
| 2 | 20/60 blend | 0.00 | -0.25 |
| 3 | 20/60 blend | +0.25 | 0.00 |
| 4 | 20/60 blend | +0.25 | -0.25 |
| 5 | 20 only | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| 6 | 20 only | +0.25 | -0.25 |
| 7 | 60 only | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| 8 | 60 only | +0.25 | -0.25 |

Fixed: 252-session z-window, 120 minimum observations, one-session BTC lag,
BIL as the defensive state. The primary is the centre of the mechanism, not
the best cell in the grid. With `tqqq_z = bil_z = 0`, there is no neutral QQQ
state after warm-up: the strategy is a pure risk-on/risk-off switch.

## 6. Falsifiers (pre-registered)

The family is killed if any of the following holds on the development window:

1. 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or 1 bp max DD >= 82.29% (the published TQQQ bar).
2. 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72% (the edge is a cost artefact).
3. The circular-shift placebo CAGR percentile is below 90%.
4. Daily-return correlation with any current family winner is above 0.95.
5. Fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent fill events.
6. Any of the three subperiods (2016-2019, 2020-2021, 2022-2023) has a
   negative CAGR.
7. A static book at the strategy's average weights matches the 1 bp CAGR
   within 1 percentage point (the timing adds nothing).
8. The future-value perturbation audit fails on any sampled date, or the
   close-to-next-open mapping audit fails (a causality bug).

The verdict is `dev_pass` only if all eight checks pass.

## 7. Expected effect

| metric | expectation |
|---|---|
| CAGR (1 bp) | 35-55% |
| max DD | 45-60% |
| Sharpe | 1.0-1.4 |
| average TQQQ weight | 0.40-0.55 |
| average BIL weight | 0.35-0.50 |
| correlation to winners | 0.40-0.70 |

If the result is in these ranges with a positive placebo and a materially
worse static blend, the BTC risk-appetite object carries information. The main
risks are (a) BTC-specific crashes that are not equity risk-off, (b) whipsaw
in bear-market rallies, and (c) the fast 20-day leg carrying most of the edge
while the 60-day-only variant is weak. The report states all three.

code:
"""family-crypto-risk-appetite -- BTC trend as an external risk-appetite switch.

Primary object: BTC-USD's 20/60-day price momentum.  Bitcoin is a 24/7,
high-beta risk asset whose trend is not a QQQ price trend.  When BTC momentum
is positive the strategy holds TQQQ; when it is negative it holds BIL.  There
is no crypto trading and no crypto position: BTC is only a daily signal series.

Causality: Yahoo's BTC-USD daily bar for date d closes at 00:00 UTC of d+1,
which is after the 16:00 ET US equity close.  The signal therefore uses BTC
closes lagged by one QQQ session, so a target set at the close of session t
only uses BTC information that was already available before that close.  The
target is filled at t+1's first bar open.

Run ``python strategy.py`` from this directory to regenerate ``result.json``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
import ext_harness as H

SLUG = "family-crypto-risk-appetite"
FAMILY = "crypto-risk-appetite"
PRIMARY = "BTC-USD 20/60-day momentum z-score, one-session lag"

END = H.END

PARAMS = {
    "windows": (20, 60),
    "z_window": 252,
    "min_periods": 120,
    "btc_lag": 1,
    "tqqq_z": 0.0,
    "bil_z": 0.0,
}

# 8-cell sensitivity grid: the primary, three threshold neighbours at the
# 20/60 blend, and the 20-only / 60-only alternatives at two settings.
PLATEAU = [
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.00, "bil_z": 0.00},
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.00, "bil_z": -0.25},
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.25, "bil_z": 0.00},
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.25, "bil_z": -0.25},
    {"windows": (20,), "tqqq_z": 0.00, "bil_z": 0.00},
    {"windows": (20,), "tqqq_z": 0.25, "bil_z": -0.25},
    {"windows": (60,), "tqqq_z": 0.00, "bil_z": 0.00},
    {"windows": (60,), "tqqq_z": 0.25, "bil_z": -0.25},
]


def _score(ext: pd.DataFrame, params: dict) -> pd.Series:
    btc = np.log(ext["BTC-USD"]).shift(int(params["btc_lag"]))
    parts = [H.rolling_z(btc.diff(int(w)), params["z_window"],
                         params["min_periods"])
             for w in params["windows"]]
    return sum(parts) / len(parts)


def make_targets(ext: pd.DataFrame, params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    s = _score(ext, p)
    return H.state_weights(s, float(p["tqqq_z"]), float(p["bil_z"]))


def _limit(end):
    return pd.Timestamp(end) if end is not None else pd.Timestamp(END)


def _check_window(ts, limit) -> None:
    last = pd.Timestamp(ts[-1])
    if last.tzinfo is not None:
        last = last.tz_localize(None)
    if last.normalize() > limit:
        raise ValueError(
            "panel extends past the development window "
            f"{limit.date()}; 2024-2026 is not loaded")


def build_weights(ts, opens, closes, params: dict | None = None,
                  end=None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Minute weights; targets at session close t fill at t+1's open."""
    limit = _limit(end)
    _check_window(ts, limit)
    ext = H.aligned(ts, ["BTC-USD"], end=limit)
    return H.to_minutes(ts, make_targets(ext, params))


def main() -> None:
    ts, o, c = H.load_panel()
    ext = H.aligned(ts, ["BTC-USD"])
    targets = make_targets(ext)
    ev = H.evaluate(ts, o, c, targets, n_placebo=100)
    st = ev["stats"]["1bp"]
    kills = H.kill_checks(ev)
    plateau = H.plateau(ts, o, c,
                        lambda p: make_targets(ext, p), PLATEAU)
    causality = {
        "future_value_perturbation": H.perturb_audit(
            ext, make_targets, cutoff_offset=1),
        "close_to_next_open_mapping": H.mapping_audit(ts, targets),
    }
    ctrl_st, ctrl_ret = H.trend_control(ts, o, c, 0.0, 0.0)
    trend_control = {
        "name": "QQQ 20/60 momentum, same binary risk-on map",
        "cagr": ctrl_st["cagr"],
        "max_drawdown": ctrl_st["max_drawdown"],
        "sharpe": ctrl_st["sharpe"],
        "corr_to_strategy": float(ev["_daily_ret"].corr(ctrl_ret)),
    }
    i = H.bt.start_index(ts, H.START)
    bench = H.bt.benchmark(c[i:, 1], ts[i:], H.BARS_PER_YEAR)
    payload = {
        "slug": SLUG,
        "family": FAMILY,
        "primary_object": PRIMARY,
        "dev": st,
        "windows": {"dev": {"1bp": ev["stats"]["1bp"],
                            "5bp": ev["stats"]["5bp"],
                            "10bp": ev["stats"]["10bp"]}},
        "window": {"dev": [H.START, H.END], "holdout": "not loaded"},
        "benchmark": {
            "tqqq_panel": bench,
            "tqqq_published_bar": H.TQQQ_BAR,
        },
        "params": {k: (list(v) if isinstance(v, tuple) else v)
                   for k, v in PARAMS.items()},
        "stats": ev["stats"],
        "events": ev["events"],
        "activity": {"fills": st["fills"], "events": ev["events"],
                     "fills_per_year": st["fills"] / st["years"],
                     "events_per_year": ev["events"] / st["years"]},
        "yearly": ev["yearly"],
        "subperiods": ev["subperiods"],
        "corr_winners": ev["corr_winners"],
        "corr_range": [min(ev["corr_winners"].values()),
                       max(ev["corr_winners"].values())],
        "avg_weights": ev["avg_weights"],
        "static_avg_weights": ev["static_avg_weights"],
        "plateau": plateau,
        "placebo": ev["placebo"],
        "causality_audit": causality,
        "trend_control": trend_control,
        "kill_checks": kills,
        "verdict": "dev_pass" if not any(kills.values()) else "fail",
        "timing": ("BTC daily closes lagged one QQQ session (Yahoo BTC bars "
                   "close after the US equity close); target set at the close "
                   "of t, filled at the first bar open of t+1; 2% band; long "
                   "only; no crypto position."),
        "notes": ("BTC-USD adjusted closes are read from data/external/ and "
                  "reindexed to the QQQ session calendar.  The development run "
                  "ends 2023-12-29 and does not load 2024-2026 prices."),
    }
    H.write_result(Path(__file__).with_name("result.json"), payload)
    print(f"{SLUG}: {H.summary_line(st)}")
    print("  10bp:", H.summary_line(ev["stats"]["10bp"]))
    print("  corr range", payload["corr_range"], "verdict", payload["verdict"])
    print("  kills", [k for k, v in kills.items() if v])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
